title: Time & Work
intro: The fastest way through Time & Work is the LCM (unit-of-work) method: let the total work be the LCM of the given days, so each worker's one-day work becomes a whole number of units. Add rates to combine workers, subtract for a leak, and divide total units by combined rate to get the time. Pipes and cisterns is the same idea with inlets positive and outlets negative; work-and-wages just splits pay in the ratio of work done.

items.name: One-day work
items.formula: if A finishes in d days, rate = 1/d (or total/d units)

items.name: Together formula
items.formula: A and B together: ab/(a+b) days

items.name: Wages
items.formula: pay splits in the ratio of work done (= ratio of rates if same time)

topics.name: Work & Efficiency
topics.details: If A does a job in 'a' days, A's rate is 1/a of the job per day. Efficiency is just rate: someone twice as efficient finishes in half the time. The LCM method removes fractions — set total work = LCM of the days, convert each person's days to units/day, then reason with whole numbers. Men-days (or man-hours) is conserved: M1 x D1 = M2 x D2 for the same job.

solved.problem: A does a job in 12 days, B in 6 days. Who is more efficient and by how much?
solved.solution: Rates 1/12 and 1/6; B is twice as efficient as A (B does 2 units to A 1).

solved.problem: A finishes in 10 days. How much work in 4 days?
15 men build a wall in 8 days. How many men for the same wall in 6 days?
A is 25% more efficient than B. If B takes 20 days, A takes?
solved.solution: A rate = 1.25 of B; time = 20/1.25 = 16 days.

topics.name: Combined Work
topics.details: To find how long several people take together, add their rates. With two workers the shortcut is ab/(a+b) days. The LCM method scales beautifully to three or more: total = LCM(days); add units/day; divide. If a third person's time is unknown but the trio's combined time is given, subtract the known rates from the combined rate.

solved.problem: A in 12, B in 6 days. Together?
A in 10, B in 15, C in 30 days. Together?
A and B together in 8 days, A alone in 12. B alone?
A in 20, B in 30; they work together 5 days then A leaves. Days for B to finish?
solved.solution: LCM 60: rates 3+2=5; in 5 days 25 units done; 35 left at B rate 2/day = 17.5 days.

topics.name: Pipes & Cisterns
topics.details: A filling pipe is a positive rate, an emptying pipe (or leak) negative. Combine them by adding signed rates; net positive fills, net negative empties. The LCM method works: set tank capacity = LCM of the pipe times, give each pipe its units/min, then divide capacity by the net rate. Watch for a pipe opened later or a leak that slows a fill.

solved.problem: Pipe A fills in 6 h, B in 4 h. Together?
A fills in 10 h, leak empties in 15 h. Time to fill with leak?
A fills in 12, B in 16; both open then A shut after 4 h. Time for B to finish?
solved.solution: LCM 48: rates 4+3=7; 4 h -> 28 units; 20 left at B (3/h) = 6.67 h more.

solved.problem: Two inlets 20 and 30 min, one outlet 60 min. All open — fill time?

topics.name: Work & Wages
topics.details: Pay is shared in the ratio of work actually done. If people work for the same time, that is just the ratio of their rates (efficiencies). Compute each person's share of the total work (rate x days worked), form the ratio, and split the wages accordingly. A partner who works fewer days earns proportionally less.

solved.problem: A in 6 days, B in 12 days do a job together for 480. Shares?
A, B, C in 10, 12, 15 days share 1500 for working together. C share?
solved.solution: LCM 60: rates 6:5:4; total 15 parts; C = 4/15 x 1500 = 400.

solved.problem: A works 4 days at rate 3 units/day, B works 6 days at 2 units/day; wage 700. A share?
A alone in 8, B in 12; they finish together and earn 1000. B share?

shortcuts: Set total work = LCM of the given days -> whole-number rates.
Pipes: inlets +, outlets -, add signed rates.
Wages split in the ratio of work done (rate x days).
Men-days are conserved: M1 D1 = M2 D2 for the same job.
mistakes: Adding days instead of adding rates.
Forgetting to subtract a leak/outlet rate.
Splitting wages by time worked instead of work done.
Averaging two times rather than using ab/(a+b).
pyq: SSC asks combined-work with someone leaving midway, pipes with a leak, and wage-sharing by efficiency. The LCM method is the safest one-method approach.

flashcards.q: A in a, B in b together?
A in 10, B in 15, C in 30 together?

flashcards.a: M1 x D1 = M2 x D2

summary: Use the LCM unit-of-work method: convert days to rates, add for teams, subtract for leaks, divide total by net rate. Two-worker shortcut ab/(a+b); wages follow work done; men-days are conserved.
